HON'BLE VIKRAM D. CHAUHAN, J. 
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned AGA for the State.

2. This application has been filed by applicant for quashing the impugned orders dated - 3.4.2023 &
26.9.2023 passed by Additional Session Judge/Fast Track Court-IInd Gautambudh Nagar in Session Trial No.- 278/2013 (State vs. Rahul & Others) arise out from Case Crime No.- 86/2011,
U/s- 498A, 304B & 323 of IPC, P.S. Phase-II NOIDA, District Gautambudh Nagar and direct the aforesaid trial Court to take appropriate steps u/s 233 of Cr.P.C. for production of Mr. Ashwani Kumar (City Magistrate) Govt. of NCT of Delhi, Lapshera New Delhi -37 & Smt. Alankrata Singh (Assistant Superintendent of Police NOIDA Gautambudh Nagar) as a defense witness in Session Trial No.- 278/2013 (State vs. Rahul & Others).

sentences.text: 3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the impugned order dated 03.04.2023 and 26.09.2023 were passed closing the opportunity of defense witnesses.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that prosecution witnesses (in question) were not produced by the prosecution and the applicant filed an application for producing the same.
Warrants were issued, however, on 03.04.2023 the order was passed closing the evidence with regard to defense witnesses.

Thereafter,
a recall application was filed which was rejected by order dated 26.09.2023.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that defense witnesses are important evidence to find the truth in the case.
4. It is to be seen that in the present case, the impugned orders were passed on 03.04.2023 and 26.09.2023.
A perusal of the order-sheet would go to show that after passing of the order dated 03.04.2023 adjournment were being sought by the applicant.
The trial court has recorded a finding that applicant is trying to delay the trial court proceedings.
5. The order-sheet would further go to show that after passing of the impugned orders the dates are being fixed and even non-bailable warrants were issued against applicant on 16.11.2023.
No reasonable cause has been shown by the applicant, as to why, the order dated 03.04.2023 and 26.09.2023 are being challenged after two years.
6. The conduct of the applicant does not inspire confidence.
The applicant is trying to delay the trial court proceedings.
Although the applicant was having knowledge of the impugned order have not challenged the same within time without any reasonable cause.
The present application is filed after two years.
7. This Court does not deem it proper to interfere in the impugned order at this stage when the case is fixed for final hearing before the trial court.
The present application filed under Section 528 BNSS is, accordingly, dismissed.

(Vikram D. Chauhan,J.) September 3, 2025 S.Prakash  Rahul Chauhan vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65952672/
